notes: Annual report of the Board of Park Commissioners for the year ending June 30, 1902, which reports the work of the three years since the last printed report. Curated: the Chain of Lakes, the Japanese Garden extension, the proposed model yacht lake, De Laveaga Dell, and the city squares the 1900 charter put under the commission.

coverage.remaining: Not placed or already on the pages: the Spreckels Temple of Music dedication (on the page), the Dutch windmill (on the page), the Goethe-Schiller monument (on the page), the bowling green (on the page), Barbour Lathrop's gift of 2,200 bamboo plants, the Children's Quarters candy stand, the spotted deer meadow and a proposed salt-water bathing pond.
coverage.note: Undated work is dated to the report year; the report covers the three years to June 30, 1902. Curated list AR1902.py.

findings.description: Digging began about November 1, 1898 on the largest and most northerly of the Chain of Lakes, opposite Fortieth Avenue: 38,000 cubic yards were dug out and piled in natural-looking mounds to the east, and the lake was given seven planted islands and a 30-foot drive around it, with a footpath at the water's edge.

findings.description: The Park Commissioners proposed an artificial lake of about six acres east of Thirty-sixth Avenue, about four feet deep and holding at least 7,800,000 gallons, filled with water pumped by windmill from new wells near the ocean, with low wharves at each end for people sailing miniature yachts.
